name: Ancestral Puebloans and Mogollon
summary: Farming peoples of the American Southwest who built great houses at Chaco Canyon and cliff dwellings at Mesa Verde. Their descendants include the Hopi and other Pueblo peoples.

knownFor.label: Chaco Canyon great houses
knownFor.note: Multi-storey stone buildings; a World Heritage Site.

knownFor.label: Mimbres pottery
knownFor.note: Black-on-white bowls from the Mogollon region.

location.value: The Four Corners region of the US Southwest (south-eastern Utah, north-eastern Arizona, north-western New Mexico, south-western Colorado).

terrain.value: Canyons, mesas and deserts of the Four Corners region.

climate.value: Dry, with hot summers and cold winters, and a rainy season in late summer.

resources.value: Maize, beans and squash, plus turquoise and clay for pottery.

disasters.value: The Great Drought: a 300-year arid period beginning after about 1130.

population.value: No regional total is given; Chacoan communities held hundreds to thousands of people.

urbanisation.value: Great houses averaged more than 200 rooms; some had 700.

disease.value: Not recorded: there are no written records from this society, and archaeology has not settled it.

migration.value: Chacoans left Chaco Canyon after a drought beginning about 1130; the article does not date later moves.

economicBase.value: Dry farming of maize with water control.

tradeRoutes.value: Macaws, turquoise and seashells from distant regions show long-distance trade.

wealth.value: No reliable estimate, though Chaco’s great houses held large stores of goods.

moneyAndTax.value: None; goods were exchanged and stored communally.

inequality.value: Some elite burials at Chaco Canyon suggest rank differences.

governmentType.value: Communities led by religious leaders and clan heads.

keyRulers.value: No rulers are known; leadership was by clan and religious societies.

succession.value: Not recorded: there are no written records from this society, and archaeology has not settled it.

institutions.value: Kivas (ceremonial rooms): a small kiva for roughly every 29 rooms, plus Great Kivas.

stability.value: Chacoans left Chaco Canyon after a drought beginning about 1130.

eliteConflict.value: Not recorded: there are no written records from this society, and archaeology has not settled it.

armyAndTech.value: Bows and arrows, and fine masonry and irrigation skills.

majorWars.value: Little evidence of war until about 1250.

territoryChange.value: Moved to the Rio Grande valley and the Hopi mesas after about 1300.

alliancesRivals.value: Not recorded; trade links reached Mesoamerica, the Pacific coast and the Plains.

scienceEducation.value: The Sun Dagger petroglyph at Fajada Butte is cited as possible archaeoastronomy.

openness.value: Long-distance trade in macaws, turquoise and seashells; Mesoamerican design influence is possible.

communicationTransport.value: The Chaco Road was built between 1000 and 1125.

languageWriting.value: Ancestors of Hopi, Zuni and Keresan speakers.

artsArchitecture.value: Pottery, masonry great houses and cliff dwellings such as Mesa Verde, and rock art.

socialStructure.value: Mostly communal, with clans and kiva groups.

sharedIdentity.value: A shared pueblo culture across many villages.

dailyLife.value: Stone and adobe apartment pueblos; maize, beans, squash.

neighbours.value: Hohokam, Fremont, later Navajo and Apache.

ideasReligions.value: Exchange with Mesoamerica spread ideas such as macaws and certain ceremonies.

colonisation.value: Spanish explorers and colonists reached the region; the article gives no colonisation date.

riseSignals.value: Farming villages grew from about 700, followed by great houses at Chaco.

peakPeriod.value: Chaco Canyon, the Pueblo II “Golden Age”, about 900–1150.

declineSignals.value: The Great Drought, beginning after about 1130.

outcome.value: Pueblo peoples continue today, including the Hopi and Zuni.

overallCertainty.value: Known from archaeology and tree-ring dating.
